title: History on the Hudson: 250 Years of Hudson County History - Battle of Bull's Ferry
description:
Date: Thursday, September 3, 2026
Time: 6:30pm - 8:00pm
Presenter: Patrick Cullen
Location: PGML: 3rd Floor | Conference Room 1

The Hudson County Office of Cultural and Heritage Affairs, in conjunction with the New Jersey Room of the Jersey City Free Public Library, presents a lecture series in celebration of the 250th Anniversary of the Declaration of Independence. For five months across the Spring and Summer of 2026, we will spend the first Thursday evening with a speaker on a wide range of Hudson County topics across our nation's first 250 years.

For the final event in the series, on September 3, Patrick Cullen presents:

Wayne's 1780 Attack on the Blockhouse

West New York historian Patrick Cullen will tell the story of Anthony Wayne's unsuccessful attack on the blockhouse that residents loyal to the British cause had constructed in what is now North Bergen and West New York. The story sheds light on the contested role of the heavily wooded areas of today's Hudson County as both side sought provisions in a "forage war."

title: History on the Hudson: 250 Years of Hudson County History - Eldorado (rescheduled from July 3)
description:
Date: Thursday, October 1, 2026
Time: 6:30pm - 8:00pm
Presenter: Lauren Sherman
Location: PGML - Fourth Floor Multipurpose Room

The Hudson County Office of Cultural and Heritage Affairs, in conjunction with the New Jersey Room of the Jersey City Free Public Library, presents a lecture series in celebration of the 250th Anniversary of the Declaration of Independence. For six months across the Spring through Fall of 2026, we will spend the first Thursday evening with a speaker on a wide range of Hudson County topics across our nation's first 250 years.

For our final talk in the series, rescheduled from July 2 to October 1, Lauren Sherman, Chair of the Weehawken Historical Commission, presents:

Eldorado – The Spectacular Late-19th-Century Amusement Resort atop Weehawken’s Palisades

Perched atop the Palisades in Weehawken from 1891 to 1894, Eldorado Amusement Park was one of the most ambitious entertainment destinations of the Gilded Age. Conceived by Hungarian impresario Bolossy Kiralfy, the 15-acre park featured a Moorish-style casino, a cliffside castle, grand fountains, music pavilions, and an enormous Roman-style amphitheater that hosted spectacular historical pageants, concerts, fireworks displays, and aerial performances.
Perhaps due to Lauren’s first career as a professional singer and actress, the Eldorado Amusement Park has fascinated her since she first saw some extraordinary 19th century photographs of this ephemeral entertainment and pleasure park. She began to research its history, delving into the life of its creator, Hungarian immigrant, and entrepreneur Balossy Kiralfy and his remarkably grand vision for sleepy Weehawken’s Palisades.

title: DIY Mosaics and Collage
description:
Date: Wednesday, September 30, 2026
Time: 4:00pm - 6:00pm
Location: Heights Branch

Join Miss Zoe and the Heights Branch staff for two hours of relaxing crafting (from 4 pm to close) with a variety of different crafts by age/ability.

Toddlers and young children may complete a small, pre-packaged mosaic craft (this activity is grab-and-go, so it may be taken home).

Kids are welcome to paint paper plate segments to create a unique mosaic (framed by two pieces of contact paper). Parents are encouraged to help with the dishing out of paint and the unsticking of contact paper.

Teens and older children may create a collage using colored pieces of paper, magazine clippings, and clippings from old books. The library will provide this material, but it is strongly encouraged to bring your own!! Each participant (over the age of 10) will be provided with one canvas and access to modge podge, paint brushes, and scissors to construct their collage. 

 

Ages 3-17 are welcome to attend this program. Children under the age of 9 must be accompanied by an adult. Adult caregivers may participate in the above crafts but will not be supplied a canvas - if they would like to collage, they can use card stock.

Registration is not necessary for this event.

title: Sensory Adventures
description:
Date: Wednesday, September 30, 2026
Time: 3:00pm - 4:00pm
Location: Communipaw Branch

🌟 Sensory Adventure with Mr. Will & Miss O 🌟

Join us for a fun and exciting special activity this month: Sensory Adventure with Mr. Will & Miss O!

Designed for Early Childhood ages 1-5, this interactive program encourages children to explore, create, and learn through hands-on sensory play.

🎨 What to Expect:

  • Sensory bins
  • Color floor tiles
  • Painting activities
  • Toys and manipulatives
  • And much more!

Children will have the opportunity to develop their fine motor skills, explore their senses, use their imagination, and make new friends in a fun and welcoming environment.

📅 Registration is Required ✅ 30 spots available

❓ Questions? Please contact William at the Communipaw Branch for more information.

We look forward to seeing you at this exciting sensory adventure!
